chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed God the Blessed the Sublime has granted me and my nation a gift that He has not granted to any other nation. This is an honor from God for us.” He was asked, “O Prophet of God! What is it?” He said, “It is breaking the fast and shortening our prayers (while we are) on a journey.” Whoever doesn’t do so has turned down God’s gifts.”
ai.seo_question: What is the special gift granted to the Prophet's nation regarding travel?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to emphasize the unique status of the Prophet's Ummah, framing the concessions of *qasr* (shortening prayers) and *qada* or *jam'* (breaking fast/traveling) not merely as legal relaxations but as divine favors (*hadiyah*) that distinguish Islam from previous nations. Scholarly tradition interprets 'rejecting the gift' as failing to avail oneself of these mercies when the conditions of travel or illness are met, thereby missing out on the specific ease granted by God. This narration underscores the practical dimension of divine mercy in Shia jurisprudence, where utilizing these concessions is seen as an act of gratitude rather than negligence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-43 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (as), on the authority of his father (as) that God’s Prophet (sw) said,

“Indeed God the Blessed the Sublime has granted me and my nation a gift that He has not granted to any other nation. This is an honor from God for us.” He was asked, “O Prophet of God! What is it?” He said, “It is breaking the fast and shortening our prayers (while we are) on a journey.” Whoever doesn’t do so has turned down God’s gifts.”
